title: Hawa: GPU flow simulation in Rhino and Grasshopper

captions.title: Hawa
captions.text: GPU flow simulation in Rhino 8 and Grasshopper.

captions.title: Open the example
captions.text: Open the supplied Grasshopper definition. Select a backend.

captions.title: Select the backend
captions.text: Auto checks the available devices. This Mac selected MPS.

captions.title: Run the solver
captions.text: The vortex completed 200 iterations inside Rhino.

captions.title: View the speed field
captions.text: The slice shows the computed velocity magnitude. Blue marks low values. Red marks high values.

captions.title: Select the device
captions.text: Choose a backend in the Grasshopper definition.

captions.title: Hawa
captions.text: Download the plugin. Open an example. Change the inputs.

title: Hawa: 3D block flow in Grasshopper with MPS

captions.title: Hawa
captions.text: Three-dimensional flow around a block.

captions.title: Define the case
captions.text: Connect the domain, geometry, physics, and boundaries to Case.

captions.title: Set the length units
captions.text: Use meters. Set the cell size to 0.5 meters.

captions.title: Run 300 iterations
captions.text: The case completed 300 iterations on MPS. The grid contains 33 × 17 × 17 sites.

captions.title: View the flow field
captions.text: The slice excludes solid cells. Each streamline follows one field snapshot.

captions.title: Pause or reset
captions.text: Set Run to false to pause. Toggle Reset to clear the state.

captions.title: Check the physical case
captions.text: The demonstration viscosity is 0.1 m²/s. Atmospheric validation remains open.

captions.title: Hawa
captions.text: Open the block example. Change its controls. Inspect the results.

title: Hawa: parametric hull search with Galapagos and MPS

captions.title: Hawa
captions.text: Parametric hull search in Grasshopper.

captions.title: Open the assembly
captions.text: Open example 09. All geometry, controls, solver nodes, and Galapagos links are in the definition.

captions.title: Change the hull
captions.text: Bow: 0.8. Stern: 0.8. Beam / draft: 2. The closed mesh volume stays at 6 m³.

captions.title: Make the ends fuller
captions.text: Bow: 0.4. Stern: 0.4. Beam / draft: 3.

captions.title: Make the ends finer
captions.text: Bow: 1.6. Stern: 1.6. Beam / draft: 1.

captions.title: Keep the test fixed
captions.text: Use the same tank, fluid, grid, and iteration count for every candidate. Enable evaluation.

captions.title: Minimize the fitness
captions.text: Galapagos controls the three shape sliders. Fitness comes from the completed CFD run.

captions.title: Run the search
captions.text: This two-minute MPS search completed one population of ten genomes.

captions.title: Restore a candidate
captions.text: Select a genome. Press Reinstate. Hawa runs the selected hull again.

captions.title: Inspect the selected hull
captions.text: Bow: 0.896. Stern: 1.461. Beam / draft: 2.586. Mesh volume: 6 m³.

captions.title: View the completed run
captions.text: MPS completed 200 iterations. The force average uses the final 20 iterations.

captions.title: Inspect the flow
captions.text: The speed slice and streamlines show the completed field around the submerged hull.

captions.title: Read the result
captions.text: Starting fitness: 3.964145. Selected fitness: 3.895586. Reinstating the selected hull reproduced its score.

captions.title: Check the limits
captions.text: The coarse grid changes the voxel volume. This short search verifies the assembly. It does not establish a real-boat resistance improvement.

captions.title: Single phase flow
captions.text: The hull is fully submerged in a viscous demonstration fluid. The model excludes waves, buoyancy, and boat motion.

captions.title: Hawa
captions.text: Open example 09. Change the shape. Evaluate. Search with Galapagos.
